full_judgment:
2. The petitioner being plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No.45 of 1995 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Cox's Bazar praying a decree for declaration of title to the land measuring an area of 1.50 acres appertaining to R. S. Khatian No.105, M. R. R. Khatian No.1, Plot No.106, Jomabondi Khatian No.157, Plot No.106 corresponding to B.S. Khatian No.7, Plot No.110, R. S. Khatian No.117, M. R. R. Khatian No.1, Plot No.110 of Mouza-Kaligonj, Police Station-Moheshkhali, District-Cox's Bazar stating in a nut shell that the suit jote belonged to Zaminder Khirod Chandra Roy and others under whom Sahar Ali, Asad Ali Mia were the rioty tenants. The R. S. Khatian was prepared in their names finally Sahar Ali and others being unable to pay rent surrendered khas possession of the said land in favour of Zaminder. The Zaminder took the land in khas possession and settled a portion of the land in favour of the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1-4, the predecessor of the defendant Nos.12,13-21, the defendant No.22 and in favour of the defendant No. 5. Thereafter settled the rest land i.e. the land of Schedule-3 land to the plaint remained as khas land which was vested to the Government by due operation of law. During S.A. operation the said land was recorded in R. S. Plot No.106 an area of 1.39 acres and in R.S. Plot No.110 an area of 11 decimals in R.S. Khatian No. 1. The plaintiff's predecessor was a sailor and that he had no land and property of his own. During the liberation war he was in West Pakistan and he was in service and after liberation of Bangladesh he came to Bangladesh. Since the predecessor of the plaintiffs have no land they improved the land of Schedule-3 and make it cultivable and used to cultivate the land. Thereafter the Government of Bangladesh Vide Settlement Case No.7 of 1973-74 settled the land of Schedule-3 in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs without receiving any salami. Subsequently an agreement was executed and registered in between the plaintiff's predecessor and the Government of Bangladesh and the possession of land was hand over to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Thereafter Jomabondi Case No.157 was open in his name i.e. in the name of Abul Kashem. The Government of Bangladesh handed over the physical possession in favour of Abul Kashem and thereafter the plaintiff's predecessor began to possess the same and have been possessing the suit land till his death and then the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land. During the B.S. operation the suit land was not recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and on 28.11.1993, the plaintiffs went to pay the rent to the office of the defendant No.26 who informed him that the B.S. recorded was not prepared in the name of the Government and also in the name of some other defendants and expressed his inability to accept the rent. The suit land is the only land of the plaintiff and that B.S. record having not been prepared in his name the title of the plaintiffs was clouded and hence the plaintiffs were compelled to file the case 

 3. The defendants No.1-5 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the Zaminder by Patta being No.105 settled the suit land in favour of the defendants predecessor Anu Mia. That thereafter more 10.17 acres of land was settled with Sultan Ahmed and others Vide Patta No.68 of 1976. The M. R. R. Khatian and B. S. Khatian was prepared in their names. The other lands were settled with Sirajul Mostafa and others by Dakhila. The M.R.R. Khatian No.137 was recorded in their names and that the settlement holders have been in possession of 3.82 acres of land in Plot No.106. Hirod Chandra had no subsisting interest in the land of Plot No.106. Thereafter the rent receiving interest was acquired by Zaminder who had no interest and the land was vested to the Government and area of 1.39 acres of land of the defendant was wrongly recorded in khas khatian No. l. That the B. S. Khatian was correctly recorded in respect of 2.51 acres of land and that the Government had no title and possession in the land of Plot No.106 and the Government was not entitled to settle any land from that plot. The Government was not entitled to settle any land from that plot and with these averments the defendants claimed for dismissal of the suit. 

 8. On the other hand the learned Counsel Mr. Md. Alamgir Kitbir appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties submits that the finding of facts whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate court is final unless it is manifestly perverse. Next he submits that the lower appellate court was absolutely right and justified in arriving at its finding and decision in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court because there is no misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record which calls for no interference by this court in revisional jurisdiction. The learned Counsel further submits that the defendant after obtaining Patta from Zaminder has been owning and possessing the suit land since a long without any interruption from any quarter. He also submits that the argument advance by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the Patta was unspecified was not correct. The Zaminder by these Pattas distributed all his khas land to different tenant and no khas land was left with the possession of the Zaminder. The learned Counsel further submits that the learned appellate court rightly observed in his judgment that if the Government would acquire the khas land of Zaminder in that case the lessee plaintiff-petitioners would produce compensation assessment roll to prove their bonafide but in the present case the plaintiff-petitioner could not produce any compensation assessment roll to show that Government acquire the suit land from the Zaminder by giving compensation. The learned Counsel to refute the argument of the lawyer of the other side submitted that with regard to preparation of record of right and correct of M.R.R. Khatian he submits that under Section 144 A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act new record will prevail upon the old record.
